item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02070","case1_error":"Applies rope loss by reducing the required length, instead of increasing purchased rope to compensate.","case2_error":"Divides the remaining points by all 20 games instead of the five remaining games.","reason":"The first reverses how loss affects required purchases; the second uses the wrong averaging denominator.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02071","case1_error":"Doubles the second country's stay for the third country instead of doubling the first country's stay for both.","case2_error":"Reports only the detour's duration, omitting the normal trip's three hours.","reason":"The first uses the wrong comparison baseline; the second answers additional travel time instead of total travel time.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02072","case1_error":"Treats 90 seconds per ear as the total ear-cleaning time, omitting the second ear.","case2_error":"No mathematical error: 120 minutes equals the explicitly stated two hours.","reason":"The second solution correctly answers the question in hours; the question does not require minutes.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02073","case1_error":"Reverses Ida's 'more than' relationship, then substitutes unsupported prices for Ida's and Patty's dresses.","case2_error":"Incorrectly defines total spending as skate cost plus remaining cash, rather than initial cash minus remaining cash.","reason":"The first reverses a comparative relationship and invents replacement values; the second misconstructs the spending balance.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02074","case1_error":"Applies only two halvings over 30 years, incorrectly labeling the first halving as the age-20 price.","case2_error":"Equates one-sixth of a day with 24 hours, ignoring the fractional duration.","reason":"The first omits a required repeated halving; the second uses a whole day's duration for a fractional day.","judgment":"different"}]}
